description:
FILED s521 (Fable, 2026-10-18 19:2x) from the s521c merge probes (review/p521c/d2-subtest-fail.sh: TAP rows identical to perl, `rc=2` vs `rc=0`), re-probed minimally (scratchpad rv/tapexit.pl): `use Test::More tests => 2; ok(0, 'x'); ok(1, 'y')` -- perl 5.40.3 exits 1 (and prints "# Looks like you failed 1 test of 2." on STDERR); PCL on the 68aeebf5 extraction AND on the s521c tip exits 0.  PRE-EXISTING.

perl's rule (Test::Builder::_ending): exit status = the number of failed tests, capped at 254; 255 when the plan and the count disagree ("Looks like you planned N but ran M") or the test died; 0 when everything passed.  `prove` / TAP::Harness read it: a failing file with exit 0 is "Dubious"-free but still "Failed"; a passing file with a bad exit is "Dubious, test returned N".  PCL's board runner and sweep read the rows, not the status, so no baseline moves -- but a program that runs its tests through `prove` or checks `$?` after `system "perl t/x.t"` gets the wrong answer.

FIX SHAPE (cl/pcl-test.lisp, the END-block plan check that #3346 moved: it already knows the counts): set the process exit status there -- failures capped at 254, 255 on a plan / count mismatch, untouched when the program already called `exit N` (perl: Test::Builder only sets it when `$?` is 0 and the test did not die); the "Looks like you failed N test(s) of M." diagnostic on the failure stream.  Probe vs perl: the reproducer; a planned-but-short file; `done_testing` with failures; a file that `exit 3`s itself; `BAIL_OUT`.  A HARNESS change: the companion `--all --quick` per batch; the sweep (test.pl's files must not move -- test.pl sets no status).  Guard rows in Pl/t/tap-assert-01.t (run_cl returns the status).  Small.
subject: The TAP layer serving Test::More EXITS 0 after failing tests; perl's Test::Builder exits with the number of failures (max 254; 255 for a plan mismatch) -- `use Test::More tests => 2; ok(0); ok(1)` is rc 1 in perl, rc 0 in PCL (pre-existing, base and tree alike); `prove` reads the status ("Dubious, test returned N"); harness
